sentences.text: Sarahsaurus holds the distinction of being the fourth basal sauropodomorph dinosaur officially identified in North America.
This mid-sized creature possessed a vertebral column that measured over 3.1 meters in length.
Its upper jaw held twenty teeth on each side, arranged with four in the premaxilla and sixteen in the maxilla.
These teeth featured serrated cutting edges, with some bearing up to twenty denticles per tooth.
Despite the sharp dentition, there is no fossil evidence indicating that Sarahsaurus possessed a beak.
The animal's spine was composed of roughly ten neck vertebrae, fourteen trunk vertebrae, three hip vertebrae, and approximately fifty tail vertebrae.
An hourglass-shaped shoulder blade distinguished the anatomy of this species.
The upper arm bone was longer than half the length of the thigh bone and bore a large, S-shaped crest extending along half its span.
The claw bone of the first finger in the hand was notably the largest of the digits.
The shin bone reached eighty-four percent of the length of the thigh bone.
Paleontologist Gregory Paul estimated the total length of the animal to be four meters with a mass of two hundred kilograms.
Sarahsaurus possessed very large and powerful hands, a feature that suggests it may have been an omnivore.
Timothy B. Rowe, Hans-Dieter Sues, and Robert R. Reisz first described the genus in 2011.
The name Sarahsaurus honors Sarah, also known as Mrs. Ernest Butler, an Austin philanthropist who funded the 'Dino Pit' exhibit.
Every known specimen was gathered from the Lower Jurassic Kayenta Formation near Gold Spring, Arizona.
Sarahsaurus shared its environment with theropods such as Dilophosaurus and Kayentavenator, as well as armored dinosaurs like Scelidosaurus and Scutellosaurus.
The ecosystem included diverse vertebrates such as hybodont sharks, lungfish, the frog Prosalirus, the turtle Kayentachelys, and the pterosaur Rhamphinion.
Early crocodylomorphs including Calsoyasuchus and Protosuchus lived alongside Sarahsaurus in the Kayenta Formation.
Coprolites and fossil tracks found in the area provide evidence of the presence of therapsids, lizard-like animals, and dinosaurs alongside Sarahsaurus.
A 2018 cladistic analysis recovered Sarahsaurus and Ignavusaurus as massospondylids, supporting the original assignment of Sarahsaurus to the genus Massospondylus.
The species belongs to the family Massospondylidae.
Sarahsaurus is classified within the dinosaur class Saurischia.
The type species of the genus Sarahsaurus is Sarahsaurus aurifontanalis.
Sarahsaurus lived approximately 199 to 182 million years ago during the Early Jurassic period.
Fossils of Sarahsaurus have been found in the Kayenta Formation, which spans northern Arizona, southeastern Utah, western Colorado, and northwestern New Mexico.
Sarahsaurus lived in an environment with a seasonal climate featuring abundant water in streams, ponds, and lakes.
By the Middle Jurassic, the environment where Sarahsaurus lived was being encroached upon by a sandy dune field that later formed the Navajo Sandstone.
